title: Maize — Fall Armyworm (FAW) and Pest Management
content:
FALL ARMYWORM (FAW) — Spodoptera frugiperda:
New invasive pest (first detected India 2018). Now major threat to maize across Karnataka.

IDENTIFICATION:
- Caterpillars: Inverted Y mark on head capsule, 4 spots in square on 8th segment.
- Damage: Window-pane damage, frass in whorl, ragged leaf edges.
- Moths: Light brown with white patches (wingspread 3-4 cm).

MANAGEMENT:
Early stage (1st-2nd instar — act EARLY):
1. NSKE (Neem Seed Kernel Extract) 5% spray in whorl at 10-15 DAS.
2. Beauveria bassiana @ 5g/L spray in whorl.

Chemical (3rd instar onwards):
1. Emamectin benzoate 5 SG @ 200 g/ha (best chemical option).
2. Spinetoram 11.7 SC @ 500 ml/ha.
3. Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC @ 150 ml/ha.
4. Thiamethoxam 12.6% + Lambda-cyhalothrin 9.5% ZC @ 500 ml/ha.

BIOLOGICAL:
- Spodoptera frugiperda NPV @ 250 LE/ha.
- Trichogramma pretiosum cards @ 1 lakh eggs/ha.
- Release Chelonus insularis @ 10,000/ha (egg-larval parasitoid).

OTHER MAIZE PESTS:
1. Ear Borer (Busseola fusca): Carbaryl 10% DP in whorl, Chlorpyriphos 20 EC @ 1.5 L/ha.
2. Aphids on tassels: Imidacloprid 17.8 SL @ 150 ml/ha.
3. Termites: Chlorpyriphos 20 EC @ 3 L/ha soil drench at sowing.

IMPORTANT: Apply FAW sprays in whorl (not on leaf surface). Wear PPE during spray. Rotate insecticide groups to manage resistance.
